title: log
intro:
Running a simulation is uninteresting, unless you can get access to the results in
one way or another. The purpose of the ’log’ component is to provide this access.
Most ’log’ models does this by writing a summary of the state to a log file.

sections.name: checkpoint
sections.desc: Create a checkpoint of the entire simulation state, suitable for later hot start.
sections.sig:
< checkpoint (where checkpoint)
                    (when when )             ; Default finished value. >

attrs.name: where
attrs.doc:
File name prefix for the generated checkpoint. The time will be appended,
     together with the ’.dai’ suffix.

attrs.name: when
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘finished’)
     Make a checkpoint every time this condition is true.

sections.name: harvest
sections.desc: Create a log of all harvests.
sections.sig:
< harvest (where "harvest.dlf")
                 (print header true)
                 (print tags true)
                 (print dimension true)
                 (print N true)
                 (print C false) >

attrs.name: where
attrs.doc: Name of the log file to create.

attrs.name: print header
attrs.doc:
If this is set to ’false’, no header is printed. If this is set to ’true’, a full header
     is printer. If this is set to ’fixed’, a small fixed size header is printed.

attrs.name: print tags
attrs.doc: Print a tag line in the file.

attrs.name: print dimension
attrs.doc: Print a line with units after the tag line.

attrs.name: print N
attrs.doc: Print nitrogen content of harvest.

attrs.name: print C
attrs.doc:
Print carbon content of harvest.
      Table columns (common):

attrs.name: stem DM
attrs.doc: Stem dry matter removed by harvest.

attrs.name: dead DM
attrs.doc: Yeallow leaves dry matter removed by harvest.

attrs.name: leaf DM
attrs.doc: Green leaves dry matter removed by harvest.

attrs.name: sorg DM
attrs.doc:
Storage organ (grains or tuber) dry matter removed by harvest. For some
        crops, only the economicly important part of the storage organ is counted.
      Table columns (if print N is set):

attrs.name: stem N
attrs.doc: Stem nitrogen removed by harvest.

attrs.name: dead N
attrs.doc: Yeallow leaves nitrogen removed by harvest.

attrs.name: leaf N
attrs.doc: Green leaves nitrogen removed by harvest.

attrs.name: sorg N
attrs.doc:
Storage organ (grains or tuber) nitrogen removed by harvest.
      Table columns (if print C is set):

attrs.name: stem C
attrs.doc: Stem carbon removed by harvest.

attrs.name: dead C
attrs.doc: Yeallow leaves carbon removed by harvest.

attrs.name: leaf C
attrs.doc: Green leaves carbon removed by harvest.

attrs.name: sorg C
attrs.doc:
Storage organ (grains or tuber) carbon removed by harvest.
      Table columns (common):

attrs.name: WStress
attrs.doc:
Number of days worth of production lost due to water stress.
     This is just a rough measure. It is calculated by weighting the water stress
     variation over the day with the amount of global radiation received in the
     same period. So water stress at noon with high radiation counts a lot more
     than water stress near sunset with low radiation. All days are counted the
     same, so water stress a day with low radiation is counted the same as water
     stress a day with high radiation.

attrs.name: NStress
attrs.doc:
Number of days worth of production lost due to nitrogen stress.
     This is just a rough measure. It is calculated by weighting the nitrogen stress
     variation over the day with the amount of global radiation received in the
     same period. So nitrogen stress at noon with high radiation counts a lot more
     than nitrogen stress near sunset with low radiation. All days are counted
     the same, so nitrogen stress a day with low radiation is counted the same as
     nitrogen stress a day with high radiation.

attrs.name: WP ET
attrs.doc:
A measure for water usage efficiency. Specifically the economic yield (storage
     organ) divided by the total evapotranspiration in the period from emergence
     to maturity or harvest.

sections.name: select
sections.sig:
< select (volume volume )                             ; Default box value.
                (summary)
                (entries entries ...)
                (from from )
                (to to )
                (when when )
                (time columns time columns )
                (parameter names)
                (active active )                        ; Default true value.
                (print initial print initial ) >

attrs.name: volume
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘box’)
     Soil volume to log.

attrs.name: summary
attrs.doc:
Component (default: an empty sequence)
     Summaries for this log file.

attrs.name: entries
attrs.doc: What to log in each column.

attrs.name: from
attrs.doc:
Default ’from’ value for all entries. By default, use the top of the soil. OB-
     SOLETE: Use (volume box (top FROM)) instead.

attrs.name: to
attrs.doc:
Default ’to’ value for all entries. By default, use the bottom of the soil.
        OBSOLETE: Use (volume box (bottom TO)) instead.

attrs.name: when
attrs.doc: Add entries to the log file when this condition is true.

attrs.name: time columns
attrs.doc:
Iff true, add columns for year, month, mday and hour in the begining of the
        lines. By default, this will be true of you have not specified any time entries
        yourself.

attrs.name: parameter names
attrs.doc:
List of string parameters to print to the table header.
        For example, if you have defined ’column’ and ’crop’ parameters for this table
        log parameterization, you can print them to the log file header by specifying
        ’(parameter names column crop)’.

attrs.name: active
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘true’)
        Add data when this condition is true. E.g. count percolation only when there
        is no crop.

attrs.name: print initial
attrs.doc:
Print a line with initial values when logging starts. By default, an initial line
        will be printed if any entry has ’handle’ set to ’current’.

sections.name: column
sections.desc:
A ‘table’ model (see 52.5, page 285) defined in ‘log-std.dai’.
   A log table for a specific column.
sections.sig:
< column (column "*")
               (parameter names parameter names ...)              ; Has default value.
               (colfid colfid )                                   ; Default cond value. >

attrs.name: column
attrs.doc: Name of column to log. Use ”*” to log all columns.

attrs.name: colfid
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘cond’)
        (colfid cond (("string-equal" "${column}" "*")
                      "")
                     ((true)
                      "${column}_"))
        Parameter description:
        File component name indicating column logged.

sections.name: Field nitrogen
sections.desc:
A ‘column’ model (see 52.6, page 286) defined in ‘log-std.dai’.
    Nitrogen input, output, transformation and content for the system.
    The intended use of this log is large scale nitrogen balance, for example reser-
voir management. It provide information about how much nitrogen is in the field
(down to a specified depth), where it is located in the field (surface, soil matrix or
in biopores), what form is has (crop, soil organic matter, or mineral) as well as the
sources, sinks and amounts of nitrogen entering or leaving the system, and trans-
formation between the four forms. It does not provide information about internal
translocation of nitrogen between surface, soil matrix and biopores, use see the ’Soil
nitrogen’ log instead for that.
    For the balances of this log to work, you must include the entire root zone
sections.sig:
< "Field nitrogen"        (summary summary ...)         ; Has default value.
                           (unit "kg N/ha")
                           (where where )                ; Has default value.
                           (entries entries ...)         ; Has default value.
                           (when when )                  ; Default hourly value. >

attrs.name: unit
attrs.doc:
Base unit.
  Table columns:

attrs.name: Min-Surface-Fertilizer
attrs.doc: Mineral fertilizer added above the soil surface.

attrs.name: Min-Soil-Fertilizer
attrs.doc: Mineral fertilizer incorporated into the soil.

attrs.name: Deposition
attrs.doc: Nitrogen added to the soil surface as atmospheric deposition.

attrs.name: Matrix-Leaching
attrs.doc:
Loss from leaching through the soil matrix below the specified depth. This
    can be negative in case of cabilary rise.

attrs.name: Biopore-Leaching
attrs.doc: Loss from leaching through biopores below the specified depth.

attrs.name: Soil-Drain
attrs.doc: Loss of nitrogen from the soil matrix to drain pipes.

attrs.name: Biopore-Drain
attrs.doc: Loss of nitrogen from the biopores to drain pipes.

attrs.name: Surface-Loss
attrs.doc:
Loss of mineral nitrogen stored above surface.
    This includes volatililzation, surface runoff, mineral nitrogen on leaves re-
    moved at harvest, and chemical transformations.

attrs.name: Min-Surface
attrs.doc:
Mineral nitrogen stored above the soil surface. This includes leaves, ponded
    water, etc.

attrs.name: Min-Soil
attrs.doc: Mineal nitrogen stored in the soil matrix.

attrs.name: Min-Biopores
attrs.doc: Mineal nitrogen stored in the biopores.

attrs.name: Error
attrs.doc:
Mineral nitrogen ’borrowed from the future’.
    This can be non-zero if the processes that remove nitrogen from some place in
    the soil are fast compared to the timestep. If this happens, you should rerun
    the simulation withh a shorter timestep. Or readjust the system to slow down
    those processes that remove mineral nitrogen.

attrs.name: Mineralization
attrs.doc: NH4 produced in the soil matrix by mineralization of organic matter.

attrs.name: Immobilization
attrs.doc: NO3 immobilized as a result of organic matter turnover.

attrs.name: Crop-Uptake
attrs.doc: Nitrogen uptake by the roots.

attrs.name: Volatilization
attrs.doc: NH4-fertilizer lost during the application.

attrs.name: N2O-Nitrification
attrs.doc:
N2O production in the soil matrix due to nitrification.
        The N2O produced is assumed to escape to the atmosphere, and will not be
        traced by the model.

attrs.name: NO3-Denitrification
attrs.doc: Loss of NO3-N due to denitrification.

attrs.name: N2O-Denitrification
attrs.doc: N2O-N released by denitrification.

attrs.name: Fixated
attrs.doc: Atmospheric nitrogen fixated by the crop.

attrs.name: Org-Fertilizer
attrs.doc: Organically bound nitrogen supplied by fertilizers.

attrs.name: Seed
attrs.doc: Nitrogen supplied in seeds when sowing.

attrs.name: Harvest
attrs.doc: Nitrogen removed as part of the harvest.

attrs.name: Residuals-Surface
attrs.doc:
Above ground plant residuals.
        This includes both exfoiliation during crop growth, and any above ground
        residuals left after harvest.

attrs.name: Residuals-Soil
attrs.doc:
Below ground plant residuals.
        This includes root death and rhizodeposition during plant growth, as well as
        the roots left after harvest.

attrs.name: Org-Surface
attrs.doc:
Nitrogen content of organic material on the soil surface.
        This does not include nitrogen in the crop.

attrs.name: Org-Soil
attrs.doc:
Nitrogen content of organic material below the soil surface.
        This does not include nitrogen in living roots.

attrs.name: Crop
attrs.doc: Nitrogen content of the crop, excluding dead leaves.

sections.name: Field water
sections.desc:
A ‘column’ model (see 52.6, page 286) defined in ‘log-std.dai’.
   Information about water input, output and content for the system.
   The intended use of this log is large scale water balance, for example reservoir
management. It provide information about how much water is in the field (down
to a specified depth), where it is located in the field (surface, soil matrix or in
biopores), as well as the sources, sinks and amounts of water entering or leaving
the system. It does not provide information about internal translocation of water
between surface, soil matrix and biopores, use see the ’Soil water’ log instead for
that.
   For the balances of this log to work, you must include the entire root zone, as
well as the biopore zone.
   Table columns:

    Precipitation: [mm]
     Total amount of water entering the system as rain and snow.

    Irrigation: [mm]
     Total amount of water added to the system from irrigation.

    Potential evapotranspiration: [mm]
     There is energy enough to evaporate this amount of water.

    Actual evapotranspiration: [mm]
     Amount of water removed by evaporation and transpiration.
     The evaporation part covers water evaporated from the soil surface, the snow
     pack, or intertercepted water on the canopy. The transpiration covers water
     removed from the soil through the root system and the stomata on the leafs.
     The actual evapotranspiration will be lower than the potential evapotranspi-
     ration when the available water is insufficient.

    Matrix percolation: [mm]
     This is the amount of water leaving the system through the soil bottom. It
     can be negative if there is cabilary rise.

    Biopore percolation: [mm]
     This is the amount of water leaving the system through biopores.

    Matrix drain flow : [mm]
     Amount of water leaving the system through the soil matrix to drain pipes.
     Note that the total amount of water in the drain pipes may be higher than
     this if you have specified the ’to’ parameter, as the whole soil profile will
     contribute to the drain flow, and only the contributions from the soil interval
     being logged is counted here.

    Biopore drain flow : [mm]
     Amount of water leaving the system through biopores to drain pipes.
     Note that the total amount of water in the drain pipes may be higher than
     this if you have specified the ’to’ parameter, as the whole soil profile will
     contribute to the drain flow, and only the contributions from the soil interval
     being logged is counted here.

    Runoff : [mm]
     Amount of water running of the surface.

        This is intended to simulate water runoff from a surface with a slop. However,
        since Daisy is a one dimensional model, the water have nowhere go to. For
        typical setups, this value will be zero.
       Biopore water : [mm]
        The total amount of biopore water in the soil interval
       Soil matrix water : [mm]
        Total water content of the soil.
       Surface water : [mm]
        Total water stored on the surface. This includes the snow pack, intercepted
        water, ponding, and water in the litter layer.

sections.name: Soil water
sections.desc:
A ‘column’ model (see 52.6, page 286) defined in ‘log-std.dai’.
    Information about water input, output and content for the soil.
    The intended use of this log is small scale water management, for example
irrigation optimization. Above ground water is considered external to the system.
The balances provided by the log will work on any subset of the soil that matches
the discretization.
    Table columns:
    Matrix infiltration: [mm]
     Amount of water entering the soil through the matrix system.
     This is the normal infiltration channel.
    Matrix percolation: [mm]
     Amount of water leaving the soil through the matrix system.
     This is the normal percolation channel.
    Biopore infiltration: [mm]
     Amount of water entering the soil through the biopores.
    Biopore percolation: [mm]
     Amount of water leaving the soil through the biopore system.
    Subsoil irrigation: [mm]
     mount of water incorporated directly into the soil.
     his include both subsoil irrigation and any water in fertilizer irectly incorpo-
     rated into the soil.
    Matrix direct drain flow : [mm]
     Flow from matrix directly to the drain pipes.
     This does not count water that flow to the drain pipes through biopores.
     Note that water flow to the drain pipes from all soil layers, both above and
     below the pipes, and even from the automatically inserted aquitard horizon
     that lies below the normal soil horizons. So if you have specified less than
     the full soil profile, that is, if you have set the ’from’ or ’to’ parameters, the
     amount you see logged here will be less than the total amount of water in the
     drain pipes.
     If the soil has no drain pipes this amount will be zero.
    Matrix indirect drain flow : [mm]
     Flow from matrix indirectly to the drain pipes.
     This only counts water that flow to the drain pipes through biopores.
    Biopore drain flow : [mm]
     Water in the interval that flows from the biopores to the drain pipes.
     Note that water flow to the drain pipes from all soil layers, both above and
     below the pipes, and even from the automatically inserted aquitard horizon
     that lies below the normal soil horizons. So if you have specified less than
     the full soil profile, that is, if you have set the ’from’ or ’to’ parameters, the
     amount you see logged here will be less than the total amount of water in the
     drain pipes.
     If the soil has no biopores connected directly to the drain, this amount will
     be zero.

       Root extraction: [mm]
        Water in the soil interval extracted by the roots.
        This number will be equal to the transpiration if the soil interval being logged
        includes the entire root zone.

       Freezing: [mm]
        Water in the soil interval turned into ice.
        This number will be zero unless the ’enable ice’ SoilHeat parameter has been
        set.

       Tillage: [mm]
        Net amount of water being added to the soil interval by tillage operations.
        This number will be zero if the soil interval includes the all the soil affected by
        the tillage operation, which is the normal case. The number will be negative
        if more water have been added than removed by the tillage operation.

       Matrix to biopores: [mm]
        Amount of water leaving the soil matrix to the biopores. This does not include
        water that flows to drain connected biopores.

       Biopores to matrix : [mm]
        Amount of water leaving the biopores to the matrix.

       Matrix water : [mm]
        The total amount of soil matrix water in the soil interval

       Biopore water : [mm]
        The total amount of biopore water in the soil interval

attrs.name: crop
attrs.doc: Name of crop to log. Use ”*” to log all crops.

attrs.name: cropfid
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘cond’)
        (cropfid cond (("string-equal" "${crop}" "*")
                       crop)
                      ((true)
                       "${crop}"))
        Parameter description:
        File component name indicating crop logged.

attrs.name: cropfid2
attrs.doc:
Component (default ‘cond’)
        (cropfid2 cond (("string-equal" "${crop}" "*")
                        "")
                       ((true)
                        "${crop}_"))
        Parameter description:
        File component name indicating crop logged. Empty if not specified.

sections.name: Crop
sections.desc:
A ‘crop’ model (see 52.15, page 298) defined in ‘log-std.dai’.
   Crop development and production.
   Table columns:

    DS : [DS]
     Development stage of the crop. 0 is emergence, 1 is flowering, 2 is ripe.

    Height: [cm]
     Height of crop.

    LAI : [m2 /m2 ]
     Leaf area index.

    Depth: [cm]
     Effective depths of root zone.

    WLeaf : [Mg DM/ha]
     Dry matter content of leaves.

    WDead : [Mg DM/ha]
     Dry matter content of dead (yellow) leaves still on crop.

    WStem: [Mg DM/ha]
     Dry matter content of stem.

    WSOrg: [Mg DM/ha]
     Dry matter content of storage organ (grain, tubber).

    WRoot: [Mg DM/ha]
     Dry matter content of roots.

    Fixated : [kg N/ha]
     Atmospheric nitrogen fixated by the crop (root biome).

    NLeaf : [kg N/ha]
     Nitrogen content of the leaves.

    NDead : [kg N/ha]
     Nitrogen content of dead (yellow) leaves still on the crop.

    NStem: [kg N/ha]
     Nitrogen content of the stem.

    NSOrg: [kg N/ha]
     Nitrogen content of the storage organ (grain or tubber).

    NRoot: [kg N/ha]
     Nitrogen content of the roots.

    water stress: [<none>]
     Highest water stress experienced in the period.
     When the root system cannot fullfil the demand of water from the canopy,
     the crop experience water stress, and production suffers.
     The value is between 0 (no water stress) and 1 (no production).

       nitrogen stress: [<none>]
        Highest nitrogen stress experienced in the period.
        When the crop nitrogen content is below a critical level, crop experience ni-
        trogen stress, and production suffers.
        The value is between 0 (no nitrogen stress) and 1 (no production).
       Phenology: [<unknown>]
        Current phenological stage.
        For most crops, this is -1 (not yet emerged), 0 (vegetative), 1 (reproductive),
        or 2 (ripe). Some crops may show other scaled, like BBCH.
